name: EU NIS2 Directive — Network and Information Security
description: NIS2 overlay for EU essential and important entities subject to Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS2). Enforcement: October 18, 2024 (EU member state transposition deadline). Applies to essential entities (energy, transport, banking, financial market infrastructure, health, drinking water, digital infrastructure) and important entities (postal, waste, chemicals, food, manufacturing, digital providers) with 50+ employees or €10M+ annual turnover. AI agent systems operating in or for NIS2-covered sectors must evidence the security measures required under Art. 21 and incident notification under Art. 23. This overlay recommends triggering on DC-GOV (public administration and government data) and DC-CRIT (critical infrastructure operational data). Operators in other covered sectors should evaluate triggering based on data classification of sector-specific operational data.

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: ICT incident notification per NIS2 Art. 23. Significant incidents require: early warning within 24 hours of detection, incident notification within 72 hours including preliminary assessment, and final report within 1 month with detailed description, root cause analysis, and cross-border impact assessment. CSIRT and competent authority are the notification recipients.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: CSIRT (Computer Security Incident Response Team) and competent national authority per NIS2 Art. 23(1). For cross-border incidents, the competent authority of primary establishment notifies counterparts through ENISA-coordinated mechanisms.

human_oversight_mandates.description: NIS2 Art. 20 requires management bodies to approve cybersecurity risk management measures and oversee their implementation. Management body members are personally liable for compliance failures. Management bodies must undertake cybersecurity training to assess risks and evaluate measures. This creates direct management accountability for AI agent security governance that cannot be delegated purely to automated systems.

notes: NIS2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555 replaced the original NIS Directive from October 18, 2024 (member state transposition deadline). Key NIS2 features: (1) Expanded scope — two-tier system (essential/important entities); (2) Management body personal accountability under Art. 20 including potential personal liability for repeated infringement; (3) Ten minimum security measures under Art. 21(2) that all covered entities must implement; (4) Incident notification — 24h early warning, 72h notification, 1 month final report; (5) Supply chain security requirements extending to ICT product and service providers; (6) EU-level coordinated supply chain risk assessment under Art. 22. Trigger recommendation: DC-GOV activates this overlay for public administration entities. DC-CRIT for critical infrastructure operators. Other covered sector entities should evaluate trigger based on operational data classification. Note: DORA applies as lex specialis for financial entities covered by both NIS2 and DORA — in that case, DORA compliance is deemed to satisfy NIS2 requirements for ICT systems in scope.
